request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

When no registration date is supplied, set it to the server's current date and return 'registrationDate' in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

agent.result_text:
Green. 

I agreed with the finding and moved the defaulting logic out of the web layer into a `@PrePersist` lifecycle callback on the `Owner` entity:

- **`Owner.java`** — Added an `@PrePersist onCreate()` callback that stamps `registrationDate` with `LocalDate.now()` only when it's null. This keeps the lifecycle rule next to the field it governs, fires exactly once on insert (so it never re-stamps on update), and applies uniformly to every persistence path through `saveOwner` — including any future callers or the V2 controller.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — Removed the inline defaulting block (and the now-unused `java.time.LocalDate` import), returning the controller to pure request adaptation and delegation.

Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: a supplied date is preserved (the callback only acts on null), and `@PrePersist` mutates the managed instance synchronously during `saveOwner`, so the create response DTO still carries the defaulted date. Both acceptance tests and the full suite pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
